clue.text: Small game hunter certain to trap like Adam's son

indicators.note: to trap means the word for certain closes around the other pieces

parts.note: bound means certain, as in 'bound to happen'
as means like, in comparisons
Seth was the third son of Adam in Genesis

explanation.surface: A hunter after small game seems sure to catch someone resembling a biblical son of Adam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to trap' is the container signal. 'Small game hunter' is the definition: the dog was bred for chasing hares and rabbits, not a hunter who is small.
explanation.definitionFit: This short-legged scent hound was bred to hunt hares and rabbits, which counts as small game.

clue.text: Law officer bends birch, say, on smuggler. About time!

parts.note: bows means bends, as in bending at the waist
a birch is an example of a tree
a runner is a smuggler, as in a gun-runner or rum-runner

explanation.surface: A policeman bends a birch rod over a smuggler, and it is high time he did.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces sit in order; 'on' and 'About' only join them, and the Bow Street Runners were London's early police force, founded in the 18th century.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bow Street Runners were an early London police force, so one member was a law officer.

clue.text: Shoot Communist leader in Israel

indicators.note: in means the leading letter goes inside the word for Israel

parts.note: Sion is a variant spelling of Zion, a name for Israel or the Jewish homeland

indicators.note: leader picks out the first letter of the word Communist

explanation.surface: A Communist leader is shot in Israel, or so the clue seems to report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes C from Communist and 'in' places it inside SION, a spelling of Zion. 'Shoot' is a noun here: a young growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A scion is a young shoot or twig of a plant, especially one cut for grafting.

clue.text: Avenger failing to impress

indicators.note: failing suggests the letters of Avenger break down and are rearranged

explanation.surface: An avenger fails to make an impression on anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' rearranges the letters of AVENGER.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave is to impress a design or lettering into a hard surface, so the infinitives match.

clue.text: A short time in, for example, Derby's environment

indicators.note: in means A and the short time sit inside the hat word

parts.note: a derby is a bowler hat, so it is an example of a hat
a bit is a short time, as in 'wait a bit'

explanation.surface: Someone spends a little while in Derby, among its surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby looks like the English city or the horse race, but here it is the bowler hat (called a derby in America); 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural surroundings in which a creature lives, which is its environment.

clue.text: Accidentally ruins map when protesting furiously

indicators.note: accidentally suggests the letters of ruins and map have been mixed up by mishap

explanation.surface: Someone accidentally spoils a map while demonstrating angrily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accidentally' rearranges RUINS and MAP together.
explanation.definitionFit: To be up in arms is an idiom for being angrily indignant and protesting loudly.

clue.text: Checker on liner shows artistic ability

parts.note: in American English checkers is draughts, so a draughts player is a checker
an ocean liner is a ship

explanation.surface: An inspector aboard an ocean liner displays a talent for art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checker' looks like an inspector; it is a draughts piece or player (draughts is checkers in America).
explanation.definitionFit: Draughtsmanship is skill at drawing, a form of artistic ability.

clue.text: Died first protecting old player

indicators.note: protecting means the outer pieces wrap around and shelter the inner letter

parts.note: ob. is the abbreviation of Latin obiit, he or she died, seen on gravestones
1st is the abbreviation for first, read here as IST

explanation.surface: Someone died first while shielding an elderly sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 in the abbreviation 1st is read as the letter I; 'protecting' is the container signal, and ob. is gravestone Latin for 'died'.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboist plays the oboe, so is a player of a musical instrument.

clue.text: Picks up eastern vehicle

parts.note: picks up means hears, as when catching a sound or a rumour

explanation.surface: Someone collects an eastern car or van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picks up' suggests collecting something, but here it means catching a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearse is the vehicle that carries a coffin at a funeral.

clue.text: Humiliate Heather in game

parts.note: to bow can mean to bring low or humble, so it stands for humiliate
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: Someone humiliates a woman called Heather during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a woman's name, but it is the plant, also called ling.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowling, whether ten-pin or on a green, is a game played by rolling balls.

clue.text: Force Georgia to be accepted by new partner

indicators.note: to be accepted by means the state's abbreviation is taken inside the partner word

parts.note: a bride is a newly married partner
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: Someone forces Georgia to be accepted by a fresh partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be accepted by' is the container signal. 'Force' is a noun here: a military unit, not a verb meaning compel.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigade is a military unit, and a military unit can be called a force.

clue.text: Mean social worker is a supervisor

parts.note: to mean to do something is to intend it
an ant is a social insect, and workers are a caste of ants

explanation.surface: A mean social worker turns out to be the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like an adjective (stingy); it is the verb. 'social worker' is an ant, a social insect of the worker caste.
explanation.definitionFit: An intendant is an official who superintends or manages, especially in historical French administration.

clue.text: Risk losing head or spleen

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the risk word is dropped

parts.note: danger means risk, as in 'at risk' or 'in danger'

explanation.surface: Risking a beheading, or perhaps a ruptured spleen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' removes the first letter from DANGER. Spleen in the old sense is bad temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Spleen means ill temper or rage, from the old belief that the organ was its seat.

clue.text: Allowance for waste is wrongly treated

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Allowance for waste is wrongly treated (4)': no parse of 'is wrongly treated' gives TRET (an anagram of treated has seven letters), and no blog or database found gives the setter's intended wordplay.
annotationWithheld.clue: Allowance for waste is wrongly treated

clue.text: Length of interval in the middle

indicators.note: in means the interval word sits inside the middle word

parts.note: the centre is the middle
a time can be an interval or period, as in 'for a time'

explanation.surface: A measurement of the length of an interval, taken at its midpoint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'of' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A centimetre is a metric unit of length, one hundredth of a metre.

clue.text: Charisma, sadly, is a thing of the past

indicators.note: sadly suggests the letters of charisma are in a sorry, jumbled state

explanation.surface: A lament that personal magnetism has sadly gone out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges CHARISMA.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaism is an outdated word or custom, a relic surviving from earlier times.

clue.text: Wild Australian orgy

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of Australian are run riot and rearranged

explanation.surface: A party in Australia that gets out of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges AUSTRALIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman winter festival of Saturn was riotous, so its name became a word for any wild revelry.

clue.text: Band outing in Kent

indicators.note: in means the outing word goes inside the region abbreviation

parts.note: Kent is a county in South East England, abbreviated SE
a trip is an outing or excursion

explanation.surface: A pop group goes on an outing in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in the south-east of England, so it gives SE. 'Band' is not a music group; it is a strip of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a long narrow band of colour or material.

clue.text: Tory delved into casual treatment of complaint

indicators.note: delved into means the Tory abbreviation digs its way inside the other letters
treatment suggests the letters of casual are handled and rearranged

parts.note: C stands for Conservative, the party whose members are called Tories

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician dug into a casual handling of a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' rearranges CASUAL to ACUSAL, and 'delved into' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An accusal is an accusation, a charge or complaint made against someone.

clue.text: Geographical feature is like this round Maidenhead

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: round means the word for like this goes around the single letter

parts.note: thus means like this, in this way
the head of Maiden is its first letter, M

explanation.surface: A geographical feature looks like this around the Thames town of Maidenhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Maidenhead looks like the Berkshire town, but it is read as 'Maiden head', the first letter of maiden. 'round' puts that letter inside THUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An isthmus is a narrow neck of land joining two larger masses, a geographical feature.

clue.text: Bill swallows note in the thick of it

indicators.note: swallows means the bill word takes the note inside itself

parts.note: ad, short for advertisement, is a bill or poster
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An invoice gobbles up a note right in the middle of the action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like an invoice; it is a poster or advertisement. 'swallows' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Amid means in the middle of or surrounded by, as one is when in the thick of things.

clue.text: It's manageable when wrongly coiled

indicators.note: wrongly suggests the letters of coiled are laid out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Something is easy to handle when it has been coiled the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges COILED.
explanation.definitionFit: A docile animal or person is easily managed and submissive, so tractable.

clue.text: Endlessly make up with husband — a yob

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the make-up word is cut off

parts.note: rouge is red make-up for the cheeks

explanation.surface: A yob wants to kiss and make up with a husband, endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make up' suggests reconciling; it is cosmetics, ROUGE, and 'Endlessly' cuts it to ROUG. A yob is British slang for a loutish young man.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough is a violent, rowdy person, a hooligan, much as a yob is.

clue.text: Insensible jazz fan needs a shot in the arm

parts.note: a cat is old jazz slang for a fan or player of the music
a tonic is something that gives a boost, a figurative shot in the arm

explanation.surface: An unconscious jazz fan needs an injection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot in the arm' suggests a literal injection, but it is the figurative boost, TONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Catatonic means in a stupor, unresponsive, so insensible to surroundings.

clue.text: Catch up on alternative trend

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the catch word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to net is to catch, as with a fish
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Catch up with the other, more fashionable direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NET into TEN in this down clue. Tenor here means general course or drift.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenor of something is its general drift or course, close to its trend.

clue.text: Slag gets drawstrings for bloomers

parts.note: to slag off is British slang to criticise harshly, as is to pan
drawstrings are cords used as ties

explanation.surface: Someone criticises a pair of drawstrings that hold up women's underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Slag (off) is British slang for criticise, so it is PAN. Bloomers are long knickers, not mistakes or flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloomers are loose women's knickers, so both name women's underwear.

clue.text: People briefly granted money for camphor

parts.note: men means people, as in 'men and women'
tho' is short for though, which can mean granted that
L stands for pound, as in the old British pound sign derived from libra

explanation.surface: People are briefly granted cash for camphor.
explanation.walkthrough: THO' is an informal short form of though, which can mean 'granted'. L is the pound, Britain's unit of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Menthol is a waxy compound obtained from mint oil, close in kind and use to camphor.

clue.text: Discovers lapse in hazard warning

parts.note: to rumble someone is British slang for to find them out
a trip is a slip or lapse

explanation.surface: Someone finds a slip in the warnings about a danger.
explanation.walkthrough: Rumble is British slang for discover or see through. A rumble strip is a ridged band on a road that alerts drivers by noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridged road strips make tyres vibrate noisily to alert drivers to an upcoming danger.
